Vulnérabilité critique affectant Cisco.

Attackers exploit a Cisco Secure Email Gateway flaw enabling file writes without login when File Reputation is enabled and scanner tools are outdated.

Attackers are exploiting a critical flaw in Cisco Secure Email Gateway that lets a sender with no login write files to the appliance's operating system, Cisco said in an advisory on Wednesday.

The attacker sends an email with a crafted attachment through the gateway and, if it succeeds, could then run commands as root. The appliance filters an organization's email for spam, malware, and other threats, and only a gateway with the File Reputation service enabled and a Content Scanner Tools package older than version 25.3.0.5525 is vulnerable.

The fix has been shipping since September 14 in AsyncOS 15.5.5-014 and 16.5.0-780, the builds Cisco listed as fixed in a hardening release that day, which the company now says covered this flaw. It also arrives as a Content Scanner Tools update, version 25.3.0.5525 or later, which installs without a software upgrade or a restart.

Cisco found the flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-76519 (CVSS score: 9.8), in its own internal security scanning and became aware of the attacks in October. The advisory does not say how many devices were attacked, who is behind the attacks, or whether the attackers obtained root on any of them.

Cisco has contacted customers of its managed Secure Email Cloud service whose devices showed "indicators of possible compromise" and says it is engaged in remediation and recovery. Vulnérabilité élevée CVE-2024-47575 affectant FortiGate.

We investigated an intrusion where attackers exploited CVE-2024-47575 to target 500+ firewalls and deploy PEERSTITCH, a memory-resident ARM64 malware.

Unit 42 investigated a multi-stage network intrusion against a telecommunications organization that occurred in September 2024, which we are tracking as cluster CL-STA-0954 (aka UNC5820). The attackers behind CL-STA-0954 achieved an initial compromise by exploiting CVE-2024-47575 against a centralized FortiManager appliance.

From that single appliance, our observations are that the attackers exfiltrated an archive containing running configurations, cryptographic material and database files containing information about more than 500 managed FortiGate firewalls. Those firewalls protected the target's own infrastructure and the networks of its clients.

Following the initial compromise, the attackers behind CL-STA-0954 demonstrated a complex level of tradecraft. Aspects of the post-exploitation activity overlap with intrusions attributed to suspected nation-state actors. Armed with the stolen information, the attackers:

The attackers exploited another vulnerability, CVE-2025-61624 , via FortiOS auto-script path traversal. This exploit facilitated the deployment of PEERSTITCH, a novel, memory-resident ARM64 malware.

PEERSTITCH leaves no persistent binary on disk, opens no listening ports and initiates no outbound network connections. Instead, it communicates through traffic generated by legitimate processes on the infected host, which makes the malware resistant to conventional endpoint and network detection.

The attackers also impersonated the FortiManager platform to pull from managed firewalls of other hosts in the targeted network.

items.detail:
Vulnérabilité élevée CVE-2026-72923 affectant Microsoft.OpenApi.YamlReader (nuget) (score CVSS 7.5).

Microsoft.OpenApi.YamlReader vulnerable to denial of service via YAML alias expansion

Applications, CLIs, developer tools, or services that parse untrusted YAML OpenAPI documents in-process may be terminated by a crafted YAML document containing nested anchors and aliases.

The impact is availability/process termination only. This report does not claim remote code execution, authentication bypass, credential exposure, privilege escalation, data exposure, or Microsoft hosted service impact.

Microsoft.OpenApi.YamlReader and Microsoft.OpenApi.Readers parses YAML through SharpYaml. SharpYaml represents aliases as shared YamlNode instances in a directed acyclic graph, so the initial parsed YAML graph remains small. During conversion to System.Text.Json.Nodes.JsonNode , aliases must be materialized as independent nodes because JsonNode instances cannot be attached to multiple parents.

Without a bound on that conversion work, a small YAML document using nested anchors and aliases can expand exponentially during conversion. With N nested anchors each referenced k times, conversion can require k^N materialized JSON nodes, leading to excessive memory allocation and possible process termination.

This is an uncontrolled resource consumption vulnerability, also known as a "billion laughs" style denial of service.

Tusk’s comments came shortly after Poland’s National Prosecutor’s Office said an analysis by the Internal Security Agency (ABW) had found Poland’s Central Anti-Corruption Bureau (CBA) — which ran the spyware program — “did not have full control over the Pegasus system” that NSO Group operated.

“The server module responsible for infecting mobile devices remained under the manufacturer's exclusive control,” the prosecutor’s office said in a press release.

The CBA also did not have passwords to access many accounts with administrative privileges, according to the press release.

“This prevented full verification of the correct functioning of individual system modules, including those responsible for data transmission and storage,” the press release said.

Incident de sécurité rapporté par The Record.

Customers of Russian travel website Anywayanyday were unable to book tickets or hotel rooms as the company responded to a cyberattack.

Russian online travel agency Anywayanyday has temporarily suspended new bookings after a cyberattack on its IT infrastructure, leaving customers unable to purchase airline and train tickets or book hotels through its platform, the company said on Wednesday.

The agency's website remains unavailable as it works to restore its systems. Previously confirmed reservations remain valid, Anywayanyday said, without providing a timeline for resuming normal operations.

“We have already taken steps to strengthen our security and are working to restore service availability,” Anywayanyday said in a statement, adding that it had found no evidence that customers' personal data had been compromised.

The company did not identify the attackers or disclose how its systems were breached.

Launched in 2008, Anywayanyday is one of Russia's oldest online travel booking services. As of 2025, the platform had partnerships with approximately 800 airlines and 330,000 hotels.

The cyberattack comes as Russia's aviation industry faces widespread disruptions following a wave of Ukrainian drone attacks targeting Moscow.

Hirudo targets eight Indonesian banking apps with patched replacements that can bypass signature, accessibility, and integrity checks.

Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed details of a new Android banking trojan called Hirudo that works by replacing legitimate banking apps with purpose-built patched versions designed to bypass security checks from inside the app itself, marking a new escalation in financial fraud.

Dutch mobile security company ThreatFabric said it identified replacements for eight Indonesian banking apps, while credential targeting in the malware spans Indonesia, China, India, Mexico, Morocco and Thailand.

"The operation combines credential theft, device takeover, screen and camera capture, and SMS theft, in combination with a fairly mature backend," Eward Driehuis, vice president of fraud engineering at ThreatFabric, said in a statement shared with The Hacker News.

Son analyse montre que la fuite ne semble absolument pas limitée à une seule salle : les 1 001 fiches examinées sont réparties entre 13 structures différentes , avec des salles Climb Up mais également des établissements MROC et SOLO Escalade.

Le volume de 151 000 profils pouvait laisser planer un doute sur le périmètre réel de la revendication. L’échantillon permet d’écarter l’hypothèse d’une fuite provenant uniquement d’un établissement local.

Parmi les 1 001 enregistrements analysés par Cyberattaque.org, nous retrouvons des clients rattachés à Climb Up Lyon Gerland, Aix Bouc-Bel-Air, Dijon, Limoges, Épinay-sur-Seine, Aubervilliers, Istres, Angers ou encore Paris Porte d’Italie .

Mais la base contient également des profils associés à MROC Villeurbanne, MROC Laennec, MROC Part-Dieu et SOLO Escalade Toulouse .

Signal de veille — The Record.

Russian-speaking Brooklyn residents began tipping off local authorities to a cryptocurrency fraud scheme three years ago, leading to an operation to take down the associated servers and domains.

Hundreds of web domains and servers were taken down by law enforcement agencies in New York City as part of an operation to stop a cryptocurrency fraud scheme targeting the Russian community in Brooklyn.

Brooklyn District Attorney Eric Gonzalez said his office worked with the FBI to seize and disrupt 241 web domains and 112 servers after the tools were used to steal millions.

The investigation began three years ago when a large number of Russian-speaking victims in Brooklyn told prosecutors they responded to Facebook ads in Russian offering investment opportunities. An investment adviser called them and walked them through the process of creating cryptocurrency accounts and transferring funds on investment platforms.

When the victims tried to take their money out, they were locked out of their accounts and told they had to pay additional fees and taxes in order to get their funds.

Several of the seized websites were made to look like legitimate investment platforms and referenced U.S. government agencies or wealthy people like Elon Musk.

Investigators found that criminals used IP addresses and infrastructure in Ukraine and several other Eastern European countries. Search warrants were executed in several countries allowing law enforcement to seize domains and servers.
